result:
I'm taking your go-ahead as a yes to staging this as a new project, since nothing is built yet. Before I write any roadmap text, here are the outcomes and tracks for you to rank.

None of these are in your own words yet. They are candidates drawn from your brief, `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`. The three research files are background for facts and costs only. I've read their headings and opening sections, not their data inventories in full.

**Outcome candidates (unranked), all from `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`**

| # | Outcome | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | A real-time vintage table of monthly CES employment: first, second and third prints, plus preliminary and final benchmarks, for total nonfarm and supersectors, SA and NSA | Total nonfarm SA vintages: small, a few thousand rows (≈560 months × ≈5 prints), available from ALFRED. Supersector and NSA vintage coverage is unknown until probed. ALFRED doesn't carry it, so it may need archived releases. FRED API limit is 120 requests/min, so the rate limit won't bind. |
| O2 | A history of revision scale at each of the four stages, year by year, for total nonfarm, with 2003 and 2020–22 marked | Cheap once O1 exists: summary statistics only |
| O3 | How much of the one- and two-month SA revision is seasonal-factor revision and how much is late sample | Model-fit cost unknown; only running it can tell. Needs NSA vintages from O1. |
| O4 | Whether collection-interval length and first-closing rate move the scale of one-month revisions | Collection days can be computed from release calendars. First-closing rates must be hand-collected, and their earliest available year is unknown. Fit cost is unknown until run. |
| O5 | What funding, staffing and sample size can and cannot be said to do to revision scale, with what is unidentifiable stated plainly | Mostly your time: roughly 45 fiscal-year values per series, hand-built from budget justifications and FedScope. Older documents may be hard to find. |
| O6 | The news versus noise share of revisions at each of the four stages, from a latent true-employment path | Fit cost unknown until run. This is the heaviest model in the set. |
| O7 | Benchmark error scale by supersector, and how wedge-back spreads it across the intervening months | Needs supersector benchmark vintages from O1. Fit cost unknown until run. |

O1 feeds every other outcome. If you want O4 or O5 estimated per supersector, with partial pooling, tell me and I'll add each as its own outcome.

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, full validation suites.

**Proposed tracks**
- **A — Vintage data and scale history (O1, O2), known progression.** Is that right, and can you name its steps from first to last? If not, I'll make it research.
- **B — Seasonal vs. sample (O3), research.** Split from the others because the decomposition stands without any driver answer.
- **C — Collection interval (O4), research.** Split from D because it is identified off within-year calendar variation, and its answer stands without the capacity question.
- **D — Operational capacity (O5), research.** Kept apart so the weakly identified, collinear covariates don't hold up C.
- **E — News and noise across stages (O6), research.**
- **F — Benchmark and wedge-back (O7), research.** Split from E because benchmark error scale by sector stands without a full four-stage news/noise decomposition.

**Choices already made**
- Python 3.14 with uv, pytest and ruff (from the repo).
- NumPyro/NUTS, Dynamax, Blackjax if needed, ArviZ and Polars (from your brief).

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists yet.

**Optional probe, only if you say yes:** fetch the ALFRED vintage listing for total nonfarm (PAYEMS) and one supersector series. This would firm up O1's coverage and size before the roadmap is written. It needs a FRED API key from you.

**Your call:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Then confirm or change the outcomes, the tracks and their kinds, and the name. Say whether you want the probe too.
